metadata.title: SonarWave | GPU Procurement, Inference Optimization & Training
metadata.description: GPU servers and AI workstations, procurement guidance, production inference and team training. Serve more users, evaluate new models and plan for service continuity.

hero.title: Get more useful AI
hero.description: Choose GPU servers and workstations that fit your AI workloads. Tune the inference software to serve more users. Equip your team to operate it with confidence. We connect the hardware, models and people so your investment delivers usable capacity.
hero.note: Buying hardware, improving a deployment or building team skills? Start with the decision you need to make.
hero.outcomesFooter: Each engagement starts with a defined problem, deliverables and success measures.

outcomes.title: Our AI needs to perform better.

businessCase.eyebrow: THE BUSINESS COST OF FALLING BEHIND
businessCase.title: AI software changes fast.
businessCase.description: New models, inference backends and serving approaches keep changing what your GPUs can do. Keeping up is a specialist job alongside running a data center. A poor stack decision can turn a major hardware investment into low utilization, rework and another unplanned purchase. We bridge that gap between hardware, AI software and the people who depend on them.

investment.title: Expensive GPUs. Too little useful AI.
investment.description: The wrong backend or serving design can leave GPUs underused while people wait for responses. Buying more hardware without finding the bottleneck can repeat the same expensive mistake.
investment.outcome: Measure useful capacity before increasing the GPU budget.

focus.title: Your specialists become infrastructure troubleshooters.
focus.description: Chasing model releases, debugging compatibility and rebuilding deployments takes time away from your team’s domain expertise. Useful new models can stay out of reach while maintenance grows.
focus.outcome: Give your team a tested platform and the skills to use it.

continuity.title: An unavailable endpoint becomes a business interruption.
continuity.description: If a provider has an outage or an overseas endpoint becomes inaccessible, dependent workflows can stop. An untested backup may lack the quality, capacity or data controls you need.
continuity.outcome: Test the alternative before the primary service disappears.

businessCase.takeaway: The outcome: more people using capable AI, less engineering time spent on avoidable rework, and a clear response when something changes.

procurement.title: Protect your
procurement.description: Before you commit to GPU servers or workstations, connect the purchase to the models and software your team needs. We review workload, inference-engine and facility requirements so your buying decision accounts for compatibility, usable capacity and total cost.

principle.title: A purchase your business can put to work.
principle.description: Bring a planned GPU system or vendor quote. Your team gets clear tradeoffs, missing requirements and the validation needed to support a buying decision.

procurement.offerDescription: A documented recommendation for what to buy, why it fits, and what to validate before ordering.
procurement.engagement: Your outcome: a buying decision backed by technical requirements.
procurement.nextSteps: GPU Procurement Fundamentals courses are available for buyers and hardware sales teams. Benchmarking, sourcing coordination and deployment are agreed in the project scope; hardware and software costs are separate.
procurement.name: GPU Procurement & System Design
deliverables: Recommended GPU, memory, storage and network specifications
Power, cooling and installation readiness checks
Vendor quote comparison, support options and total cost
Compatibility risks, validation steps and acceptance criteria

inference.title: Put better AI
inference.description: Turn a promising AI deployment into a service people can depend on. We select and tune the inference engine for your models, GPUs and real user demand, then plan upgrades and recovery. Get more useful throughput from your investment while your specialists focus on their own work.
inference.successMeasures: Agree the baseline and targets before delivery: useful response quality, users served at once, cost per workload and recovery time. Implementation, handover and any ongoing support have a defined scope.

models.title: The right engine
models.description: A model that runs is not necessarily a model that runs efficiently. Different architectures can need specialized engine support, optimized GPU kernels and serving configurations. We benchmark the options and tune the model–engine–GPU combination for higher throughput within your quality and latency targets, then reassess as models and engines change.
points: Model architecture, engine version and GPU compatibility assessment
Supported kernel, precision, batching, caching and parallelism optimizations
Throughput, response-time and quality comparisons under realistic load
Tested engine upgrades, staged rollout and rollback

continuity.eyebrow: A PLAN B FOR YOUR AI SERVICES
continuity.title: Keep essential workflows
continuity.description: Plan for provider outages, access restrictions and failed upgrades. We assess alternative providers or locally hosted models and test how critical workflows switch over, including the capacity and functionality available during recovery.
points: Fallback model or provider validation and failover testing
Recovery targets, operating procedures and staff handover

stages.title: Match the engine to the model.
stages.description: Model architectures and inference engines evolve together. Compare supported engines and versions for your models and GPUs, including specialized optimizations, quality, licensing, latency and throughput.

stages.title: Make capacity usable.
stages.description: Tune precision, batching, caching and parallelism where the model and engine support them. Load-test realistic requests and concurrent users to improve throughput within your quality, response-time and memory requirements.
stages.deliverable: Load-test results, serving configuration and capacity plan

stages.title: Roll out with a recovery path.
stages.description: Validate model and software updates before release. Plan staged rollouts, health checks and rollback, and test fallback options for a failed model service or an unavailable external provider.

stages.title: Equip your team to operate.
stages.description: Establish monitoring, access controls, vulnerability checks and operating procedures. Train your staff to recognize capacity limits, handle incidents and assess the next model or backend change.
stages.deliverable: Operational handover, staff training and agreed support scope

training.title: Make the investment
training.description: Reduce dependence on a few specialists and help staff put AI to productive use. Our courses and practical sessions build technical confidence, while sales enablement helps customer-facing teams identify relevant upgrades and additional services. The outcome is stronger internal capability and better-informed sales conversations.

technical.title: Turn specialist knowledge into everyday capability.
technical.description: Close the gap between maintaining GPU hardware and running AI models well. Build the skills to assess software changes, recognize bottlenecks and follow release and recovery procedures.
points: GPU procurement, model–engine compatibility and serving fundamentals
Practical capacity, deployment and incident scenarios
Training scoped to your team’s roles and current knowledge

items.question: Who is this for, and when should we start?
items.answer: For leaders responsible for AI investment, operational continuity and workforce capability, along with the data-center, procurement, engineering and sales teams delivering those goals. Start before a GPU purchase, when a deployment struggles with demand, or when model upgrades and external dependencies create business risk.

items.question: Is this advice only, or do you help deliver the outcome?
items.answer: We provide procurement guidance and courses, and we also scope hands-on system design, hardware sourcing, production inference implementation, testing and staff handover. Any ongoing support is agreed separately. We define the baseline, deliverables and success measures together so the engagement is tied to an operating result.

items.question: How will we know the investment is working?
items.answer: We agree measures suited to the goal before work starts. For production inference, these can include task quality, concurrent users, response times, GPU utilization, cost per workload and recovery time. For training, we agree role-specific learning goals and practical demonstrations. Results are assessed against your starting point and the agreed scope.

items.question: Do you help source GPU servers and AI workstations?
items.answer: Yes. We help specify and source GPU workstations for AI development and GPU servers for training and inference through OEMs, resellers and specialist builders. System design, benchmarking, sourcing and deployment are scoped to the project. Availability and delivery timelines are confirmed with vendors.

items.question: Can you improve an existing AI deployment?
items.answer: We can assess an existing deployment before you commit to more hardware. We establish a performance baseline and identify opportunities to improve capacity. Changes are tested against throughput and response-time targets so you can decide whether to optimize, reconfigure or expand. The workload, measurements and scope are agreed before work begins.

items.question: Do you train technical staff and customer-facing sales teams?
items.answer: Yes. We offer courses and practical training for data-center staff, buyers, technical teams and hardware salespeople. Sales teams learn to connect a client’s business goals to model, inference-engine and hardware requirements, explain how procurement affects the software stack, and identify useful capacity or service upgrades. Technical training covers operating, optimizing and updating the serving environment.

items.question: How do you scope and price the work?
items.answer: After the initial conversation, we define the deliverables, responsibilities, acceptance measures and fee in a proposal. Procurement advice, implementation, training and any ongoing support have clear scopes. Hardware purchases, software licences and cloud usage are separate, with costs agreed before work begins.
